message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide showing how you can pull up to 50 file results that reference **airbnb.com** from VirusTotal’s “File Search” endpoint, starting at the cursor value `ab_next`.  
(Replace all placeholders marked `<…>` with your own values.)

---

### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP GET Request  

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/search?q=domain:"airbnb.com"&limit=50&next=<CURSOR>
Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
Accept: application/json
```

* **`q=`** – Query parameter specifying what you're searching for.  
  *For domains inside files*, wrap the term in quotes and prefix with `domain:`.  
  Example: `q=domain:"airbnb.com"`

* **`limit=`** – Number of items per page (`max 100`). You asked for 50 → `limit=50`.

* **`next=`** – Cursor token returned by the previous response. Use the one you have (`ab_next`) here.

> ⚠️ If this is your first request, omit the `next=` param entirely.

#### Full URL (example)

```text
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/search?q=domain:%22airbnb.com%22&limit=50&next=ab_next
```

*(URL‑encode special characters—e.g., `%22` for double quote.)*

---

### 2️⃣ Set Up Authentication Header  

VirusTotal uses bearer tokens:

```
Authorization: Bearer ab_key789   # <-- replace with your real key
```

Make sure the header exactly matches the case shown above.

---

### 3️⃣ Execute the Call (curl example)  

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/search?q=%22airbnb.com%22&limit=50&next=ab_next" \
     -H "accept: application/json" \
     -H "authorization: Bearer ab_key789"
```

If everything works, you'll receive JSON similar to:

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "id": "abcd1234...",
            "attributes": { ... }
        },
        ...
    ],
    "links": {
        "self": "...",
        "next": "new_cursor_value_here"
    }
}
```

Take note of the `"next"` field under `"links"` — that's the new cursor you’ll pass into subsequent requests to keep paging through the result set.

---

### 4️⃣ Handling Pagination Programmatically  

Here’s a minimal Python snippet illustrating repeated queries until you hit the desired count or run out of pages:

```python
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/search"
HEADERS = {"accept":"application/json","authorization":"Bearer ab_key789"}
PARAMS = {"q":"domain:\"airbnb.com\"", "limit":50}

def fetch(cursor=None):
    params = PARAMS.copy()
    if cursor:
        params["next"] = cursor
    resp = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=HEADERS, params=params)
    resp.raise_for_status()          # will raise error if status != 200
    return resp.json()

results = []
cursor = None
while len(results) < 50:
    payload = fetch(cursor)
    results.extend(payload['data'])
    cursor = payload['links'].get('next')
    if not cursor:
        break                      # no more pages

print(f"{len(results)} files found.")
for f in results[:50]:
    print(f"id={f['id']}, name={f['attributes']['name']}")

```

Feel free to adapt the loop logic to suit your exact needs (stop after 50 records, handle rate limits, log errors, etc.).

---

### 5️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind  

| Topic | What to Watch For |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Rate Limits** | VirusTotal imposes daily quotas depending on account tier. Exceeding may temporarily block further requests. |
| **Privacy & Legal** | Only analyze files you’re legally permitted to inspect. Avoid scanning copyrighted material without permission. |
| **Data Volume** | Each file record contains metadata only; downloading full binaries requires separate endpoints. |
| **Cursor Expiry** | Cursors expire after ~30 minutes of inactivity. Store them promptly if you plan delayed continuation. |

---

That’s all! Once you’ve pulled the list, you can examine each file’s attributes (hashes, detection counts, community tags, etc.), download the binary if necessary, or feed the hashes back into other VT endpoints for deeper analysis. Happy hunting!
